nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) was used for normative modeling. The model was previously trained on a reference cohort of 33,072 healthy controls using age and sex as covariates, then adapted using transfer learning with a local adaptation dataset (n=20 cognitively normal adults). The HBR approach uses partial pooling methodology to handle multi-site data, incorporating structural dependencies among model parameters by sharing a common prior distribution.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Hierarchical Bayesian regression proposed by Kia and colleagues was used, given its advantages over other methods for normative modeling of real-world clinical data

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Regional cortical thickness was the response variable. Cortical reconstruction and volumetric segmentation were performed using FreeSurfer 6.0, with 148 cortical parcellations (74 in each hemisphere) based on the Destrieux atlas. Z-scores were generated for each brain region, with outliers defined as z < -1.96 (bottom 2.5% of normative range).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Hierarchical Bayesian regression was previously trained on the reference cohort... using age and sex as the covariates to index population variability in cortical thickness across all 148 regions of interest (ROIs)

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex were used as covariates to index population variability in cortical thickness. Site effects were handled through hierarchical Bayesian regression with transfer learning adaptation (adaptation dataset of 20 cognitively normal older adults scanned at the same site as the clinical cohort). The HBR approach accounts for both additive and multiplicative batch effects across sites.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: Hierarchical Bayesian regression was previously trained on the reference cohort... using age and sex as the covariates to index population variability in cortical thickness across all 148 regions of interest (ROIs). This model was then optimized using cortical thickness data from controls scanned at the same acquisition site as the clinical cohort (n = 20).
